Description: Within a customer tenant, prompt injection or jailbreak causes an agent to take unintended tool actions or surface sensitive data via model output. Single-tenant deployments architecturally prevent cross-tenant data exposure.
Treatment Decision Notes: Emerging risk category. Mitigations are evolving per industry guidance (OWASP LLM Top 10, NIST AI RMF). Active monitoring and threat modeling are appropriate.
Impact Justification: Cross-tenant data leakage via model behavior would be a customer trust event and potentially a breach notification trigger.
Likelihood Justification: Prompt injection and jailbreak techniques are widely published. The AI threat landscape is active and evolving.
Residual Impact Justifcation: Single-tenant deployments architecturally prevent cross-tenant exposure. {{MODEL_PROVIDER}} zero-retention prevents model fine-tuning leakage. Blast radius is contained to a single customer if exploited.
Residual Likelihood Justification: AI threat landscape is less mature than conventional appsec. Defensive controls continue to mature in line with industry guidance.

Description: Targeted or opportunistic phishing succeeds at obtaining an employee credential or MFA factor.
Treatment Decision Notes: Phishing remains a realistic vector even with MFA. Training is high-leverage and low-cost.
Impact Justification: Successful phishing could grant access to {{CLOUD_PROVIDER}}, {{DATA_STORE}}, or {{VCS}} depending on the target.
Likelihood Justification: Phishing campaigns against SaaS employees are constant. Volume and sophistication continue to rise, but {{IDP}} account takeover and phishing protections are world class.
Residual Impact Justifcation: Phishing-resistant MFA blocks credential phishing for protected accounts. Least-privilege limits damage if a non-privileged account is compromised.
Residual Likelihood Justification: Advanced phishing techniques may bypass some MFA factors. Sophisticated attackers remain a residual concern even with strong controls. Risk closes out with passkeys or phishing-resistant MFA on federated IdP platform

Description: Subprocessor (AI provider, cloud platform, database) suffers a breach exposing ACME customer data they process.
Treatment Decision Notes: Vendor breach risk is inherent to SaaS dependencies. Self-hosting would not be cost-justified relative to residual risk
Impact Justification: Breach at {{MODEL_PROVIDER}}, {{CLOUD_PROVIDER}}, {{DATA_STORE}}, or {{DATA_STORE}} could expose ACME customer data they process.
Likelihood Justification: Major cloud and AI providers maintain strong security postures. SOC 2 opinions for all critical vendors are clean for the current period.
Residual Impact Justifcation: Even with strong vendor diligence, a major vendor breach would still expose data. No compensating control fully eliminates supply-chain exposure.
Residual Likelihood Justification: Annual SOC 2 review and tier-based diligence per Vendor Management Policy. DPA on file for processors of customer data.

Description: Financial fraud or management override of controls (BEC, fraudulent invoices, {{SECURITY_OWNER}} bypassing access or change controls for personal benefit).
Treatment Decision Notes: Out-of-band confirmation for payment changes and PR-based change management are low-cost controls
Impact Justification: Successful BEC or invoice fraud could divert significant funds.
Likelihood Justification: Small team with mutual visibility. CEO and COO share visibility into vendor and financial decisions.
Residual Impact Justifcation: Small-team mutual visibility is the strongest natural control but is not infallible. Management override remains a residual exposure that mitigating controls reduce but cannot fully eliminate.
Residual Likelihood Justification: Out-of-band or two-person confirmation for vendor payment changes. Annual privileged-access review provides an independent check.

Description: {{SECURITY_OWNER}} as sole owner of security policy, IR, vendor reviews, and access reviews, becomes unavailable (departure, incapacity, leave).
Treatment Decision Notes: Documentation and CEO break-glass is appropriate for the current organizational scale. Full role redundancy is not cost-justified.
Impact Justification: {{SECURITY_OWNER}} unavailability would slow IR, vendor review, and access provisioning until coverage is established.
Likelihood Justification: Low base rate. Planned absences are coordinated.
Residual Impact Justifcation: Documentation reduces single-point-of-failure. CEO break-glass is partial. Cross-training reduces but does not fully eliminate single-point-of-failure exposure.
Residual Likelihood Justification: Policies and procedures are documented and accessible. CEO has alternate access to security@ and break-glass admin.

Description: Major {{CLOUD_PROVIDER}} regional outage or managed service incident causes extended downtime beyond the 24h RTO.
Treatment Decision Notes: Multi-region active-active is not cost-justified at current scale. 24h RTO is an internal recovery target unless a contract specifies otherwise.
Impact Justification: 24h RTO can absorb most provider incidents. An extended regional outage would affect customer trust but not data integrity.
Likelihood Justification: {{CLOUD_PROVIDER}} regional outages are rare and typically short. ACME product is non-life-safety.
Residual Impact Justifcation: Managed services restore quickly. Observability data loss is non-blocking for service recovery.

Description: Current or departed employee uses retained access to exfiltrate, modify, or expose customer or company data.
Treatment Decision Notes: Offboarding rigor and access reviews are standard practice. Cost is low.
Impact Justification: An insider with production access could exfiltrate the full customer dataset or sabotage production.
Likelihood Justification: {{TEAM_SIZE}} team with high mutual visibility. Departures are rare and coordinated.
Residual Impact Justifcation: Least-privilege limits damage. Offboarding Checklist revokes access within 1 business day of departure.
Residual Likelihood Justification: Small team size and tight access controls limit opportunity. Cultural and contractual obligations reinforce these controls.

Description: Repository accidentally made public, {{VCS}} Actions secrets leaked in logs, database, or {{CLOUD_PROVIDER}} Storage bucket configured public.
Treatment Decision Notes: IaC and PR review convert most misconfig risk to a code review problem rather than an ad-hoc operational risk.
Impact Justification: Public repo or open bucket could expose source code depending on what was misconfigured.
Likelihood Justification: Misconfiguration is the most common cause of cloud data exposure incidents industry-wide.
Residual Impact Justifcation: Encryption at rest, branch protection, secret scanning, and push protection add depth. Even if an artifact is exposed, useful secret extraction requires further work.
Residual Likelihood Justification: IaC-managed config and PR review reduce human-error misconfigs. Secret scanning catches credentials before push.

Description: Third-party dependency vulnerability is exploited or supply chain attack injects malicious code into production builds.
Treatment Decision Notes: Automated scanning is low cost. Patching cadence is the operational cost.
Impact Justification: Exploited dependency vulnerability could lead to RCE in ACME application. Supply chain attack could inject malicious code into production builds.
Likelihood Justification: Critical vulnerabilities in popular packages are disclosed regularly. Supply chain attacks are increasing.
Residual Impact Justifcation: Containerized runtime limits blast radius. Managed databases are not directly exposed.
Residual Likelihood Justification: Automated dependency scanning is enabled. PR scanning blocks merges with known critical CVEs. Patch timelines follow the Patch Management Policy.

Description: Company laptop is lost, stolen, or compromised while holding credentials.
Treatment Decision Notes: Full-disk encryption and password controls are standard endpoint hygiene.
Impact Justification: A compromised laptop with active session tokens could grant short-window access to production systems.
Likelihood Justification: Devices are securely configured and are not routinely left in unattended public spaces.
Residual Impact Justifcation: Session tokens are short-lived. Production access requires MFA.
Residual Likelihood Justification: Full-disk encryption, passwords, and screen lock close the realistic loss vector quickly.

Description: Customer conversation data is retained in database and analytics platforms beyond the deletion window committed in the Privacy Policy.
Treatment Decision Notes: Privacy commitments are external. Failing to meet them creates contractual and regulatory exposure.
Impact Justification: Customer data over-retention could be a Privacy Policy breach with potential CCPA implications.
Likelihood Justification: Manual deletion process is in place. Retention windows are short.

Description: Attacker obtains an employee credential through phishing, reuse, malware, or session theft and accesses customer AI conversation data in vendor SaaS platform.
Treatment Decision Notes: MFA and least-privilege close the realistic attack vector. Mitigation cost is low. Detective controls already exist.
Impact Justification: A compromised credential could access {{DATA_STORE}}, {{CLOUD_PROVIDER}}, or {{DATA_STORE}} depending on the user's role, potentially exposing all customer AI conversation data.
Likelihood Justification: Phishing volume against SaaS employees is high. Credential reuse remains common across the industry.
Residual Impact Justifcation: Least-privilege scoping prevents a compromised engineer credential from granting production database access. Encrypted data limits offline exposure.
Residual Likelihood Justification: MFA on all corporate tenants, federated to {{IDP}}, closes the credential-reuse vector. Hardware keys for privileged access raise the bar against phishing.

Description: External or internal actor gains direct access to {{CLOUD_PROVIDER}} IAM, {{SECRETS_MANAGER}}, or production resources outside normal access controls.
Treatment Decision Notes: IAM least-privilege and audit logging are standard cloud hygiene with minimal incremental cost.
Impact Justification: Direct {{CLOUD_PROVIDER}} access could modify IAM, exfiltrate {{CLOUD_PROVIDER}} Storage or {{SECRETS_MANAGER}} values, or alter production configuration.
Likelihood Justification: {{CLOUD_PROVIDER}} IAM is federated to {{IDP}}. No standalone passwords exist on the project. The console is not exposed externally.
Residual Impact Justifcation: {{CLOUD_PROVIDER}} Audit Logs allow issue identification and managed services limit lateral movement.
Residual Likelihood Justification: IAM least-privilege, MFA, and audit logs make undetected entry difficult.

Description: Financial loss from a cybersecurity incident exceeding company reserves due to absence of cyber liability insurance.
Treatment Decision Notes: Insurance is a transfer mechanism with material recurring premium at small scale. The financial exposure has been considered and accepted by the {{SECURITY_OWNER}} with named re-evaluation triggers: (a) execution of an enterprise customer contract that requires cyber coverage, (b) processing of regulated data (PHI, PCI), or (c) the next annual risk review, whichever occurs first.
Impact Justification: A cybersecurity incident with material customer or operational impact could create financial exposure (remediation, notification, legal fees, potential customer claims) that exceeds company reserves without insurance to offset.
Likelihood Justification: Low base rate at current scale. ACME is pre-customer-revenue for enterprise tiers and processes no regulated data; preventive and detective controls reduce the probability of an event reaching this severity.
Residual Impact Justifcation: Without insurance, the residual financial exposure from a significant incident remains on the company balance sheet. Preventive controls reduce probability but do not transfer financial risk.
Residual Likelihood Justification: Underlying security controls (MFA, least-privilege, encryption, IR program, vendor reviews) reduce the likelihood of a material incident. The named re-evaluation triggers ensure the acceptance is revisited when conditions change.
